utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner, assisted, as always, by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friend from the OTP, everybody in the courtroom, and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson, assisted by Lejla Gluhic for the Defence of General Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will always remind you, sir, that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Thank you. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hasanagic. Yesterday we stopped while discussing your attempts to put -- place the Mujahedin under your control.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you stopped me while I explained how the Mujahedin came to my division. And, Your Honours, if I may explain something.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every -- their visit to the commander was pregnant with misunderstanding. First of all, we had in the division command women who worked in the operations, in finances, and every time they required the women to be moved out and they wanted a Cafir in the commander. They wanted to see whether there were Croats and Serbs in the command. Of course we had, and I was proud of that fact. Another constant problem is that they were enemies of smoking, and this engendered conflict every time they visited the command and unit. And in pauses between fighting, there was alcohol sloshing around. I could not control a front line of 50, 60 kilometres and more than 12.000 people in my division. They showed mistrust to me, and I didn't want -- didn't want to change my views in terms of the composition of my command and the establishment of my command and the daily work and life of my command. And, of course, gradually they became ever more distant from me. And an intelligence of the 3rd Corps that was sent to the General Staff says that they had support from the then-municipal authorities of Zavidovici and the Muslim clergy. At that time, I was the commander and I did not want to admit that I was afraid, but my security guards and people in my immediate vicinity knew that. And today I can tell you, Your Honours, frankly I was afraid of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hasanagic. I did not interrupt you yesterday. It was force majeure. We had to stop because of some other engagements of the Chamber. Thank you for this explanation. I will try to elaborate on what you just said. Now I would like the witness to take a look at PT2095, please. And before we see the document on the screen, for the record, Your Honours, I would like to say that this is a document by the 35th Division command. It is an order concerning a team for monitoring and controlling combat activities. Witness, now I would like to ask you to take a look at this document when it appears on the screen. It is document PT2095.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't see it on the screen. Ah, thank you. Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please focus your attention first on item 1 of this document -- I mean first page. And please confirm that this is a document by the 35th Division. And now I would like the second page of both versions be shown so that we can see where the signature is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this would be page 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's go back to the first page of this document. It is evident that you ordered that teams for monitoring and controlling combat operations to be established. Do you agree that this is what it says under the "I order"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's teams for monitoring and controlling and assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and assistance. Okay. Thank you. And it says here that you specified a team of your officers, including Nesad Sabic, chief of staff, to assist the detachment. Your Honours, could you please take a look on page 1. There is part of the relevant section. And if we can see the second page so that the Bench may follow. Page 2 of the English version, please. It says here that you ordered some assistance to be provided, but it is true, is it not, Mr. Hasanagic, that the El Mujahedin Detachment never admitted Sabic in -- onto their premises? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what my chief of staff told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Simply they did not accept assistance from you or your officers. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at item 2, the tasks and missions of those teams. Your Honours, in the English version, you must take a look at page 3, the top of the page. Good. Now, Mr. Witness, I see that you are reading those tasks outlined under item 2. If I were to interpret those tasks, it seems that your tasks were supposed to monitor, direct, and coordinate the work of units, departments, organs. Do you agree that this is stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have to slow down for the transcript. Mr. Hasanagic, do you agree that this would entail them to monitor, direct, and coordinate the work of the El Mujahedin Detachment along with the others? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But this is not what your team of officers succeeded in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we did not know what the departmental organs of that unit were, because we did not know anything about the establishment of that detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the other hand, they did not permit your chief of staff to come into their premises, to monitor all these. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, a team of your officers could not control the implementation of the security measures orders on the part of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Would I be correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the same reason, because we did not know whether they had the departmental organ there and who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I tender this document into evidence and may it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit number will be 487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to see document D419.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Hasanagic, may I say for the record that this is a document, an order of the 35th Division's command from the command post Klek dated 27th of May, 1995. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It seems that the document bears your signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the document concerns connecting an engineering configuration of the newly reached lines? It is a brief document. Please read through it so that I don't encumber the record and transcript.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the basis of --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please read it silently.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But please pay particular attention to item 5. And do you agree that it says that: "By 20.00 hours on the 27th of May, 1995, a detailed combat report on combat activities during that date should be delivered. In it, it should be reported on the use of materiel and technical equipment, munitions, explosives, requests of supply, et cetera? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that under item 2, it says that newly reached lines should be fortified; engineering work had to be done; and they ought to be linked with the firing system and link up the gaps? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you never received this detailed combat report by the deadline specified; meaning, 20.00 hours on the 27th of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither did the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to find out: Did you never receive that detailed report from all these people that -- to whom this order was addressed? The order was addressed to the 3rd Corps command El Mujahedin Detachment, 328th Brigade, 329th. All those people? Or which -- who didn't -- from whom did you not receive this detailed report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not receive that report from the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you receive it from the others, the other addressees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I did, but I can't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I stopped at discussing these lines and their -- the engineering work on them. Is it -- it's true, is it not, Mr. Hasanagic, that the El Mujahedin Detachment never followed your orders when it came to engineering fortifications? They proceeded at their own will. I mean, the detachment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had no engineering units, so they went about doing engineering work to the best of their abilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, but what I'm interested in is whether the detachment followed your orders in this respect, in respect of engineering tasks. Did they or did they not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me rephrase. It says here: "Fortify lines reached, do engineering work on them, link up the firing system and the gaps." This is my question to you: Did the El Mujahedin Detachment upon receiving this order from you do the engineering work on the areas where they engaged in combat and linked up with the firing system -- and did they link up with the firing system of your units?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. They were supposed to do that, but I don't remember whether they did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 488, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can put this document aside. Can the witness be shown PT2117.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: General, while we are waiting for the next document, I'd like to ask you if the El Mujahid Detachment ever asked for engineering support from the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And did you give it to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, Mr. Hasanagic, can you look at this document. For the record, let me specify that this is a report from the command of the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion, sent to the 35th Division - that's to say, to your command - and concerns Proljece 1995. The document is dated the 28th of May, 1995. Can the witness look at page 2, at the signature block. Let me ask you this: Commander Captain Smajo Saric is in the signature block. Does this name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was the commander of the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion, and this is the -- a unit on the strength of the corps -- a corps unit. Or rather --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: A corps unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see that a document is sent to the 35th Division. I would like you to turn to the last paragraph of item 1. If we could go back to page 1 in Bosnian. I'd like to look at the last sentence in item 1 but just above subitem (a). It says here: "Problems encountered in the execution of the task were as follows," and their various problems are listed, of which the 35th Division is being put on notice. Take a look at these problems, please. Concerning the El Mujahedin Detachment, it says that guides were not designated who should have taken units to certain sectors. Do you agree that this is what it says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that members of this detachment did not allow for the sector to be entered into and for the positions there to be taken up in a timely fashion. As a result, the units of the 35th Division came under artillery fire from Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of the 35th Division but of the 2nd Mechanised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Perhaps I misunderstood this. Next it says that the unit, under (b), says that because of the arbitrariness in the conduct of that unit, they suffered losses in the battalion. It also says that due to the requests of the El Mujahedin Detachment, the mission could not be carried out at night-time and it had to be put back for the following day. Do you agree that this is what it says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question in connection with this: Do you agree that this document shows that the detachment did not in fact fit into the prescribed command-and-control system of the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Would you agree with this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordinated action between units of the same level in a combat activity involved the coordinated action between the manoeuvre battalion and the detachment. I am looking at the document now, and I see that they were unable to find an agreed course of action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Leaving this document aside for the time being, tell us, you had experience with the El Mujahedin Detachment on the ground. Would you agree with the statement that the detachment did not fit into the command-and-control system precisely in the way as described in this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were given assignments, just as other units were; however, they did not execute these assignments in the way that they had been asked to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They preferred carrying out assignments on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even though they did not wish to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: Even if -- and if they did not want to engage in a certain action at a certain point in time, they simply didn't go about doing it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if they decide not to engage in an action, this is their decision and one could not give them any further orders on that matter. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 489, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness be shown Exhibit 447. Let me state for the record that this is an order for engineering support to the 35th Division dated the 15th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of his examination, the Prosecutor showed you this document, Mr. Hasanagic. I want you to have another look at it. You do remember this document, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Look at item 2 again, where it says: "tasks of subordinate units" which include tasks to the El Mujahedin Detachment, among others. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have to say that the operative, such as he was and that I had, he said -- he wrote that these were tasks to units. He doesn't say which ones. And as a rule, one would not need to put "subordinate unit." That goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is that right that this is something you referred to in answering questions to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I please ask you to turn to the text below the heading that says "El Mujahedin Detachment." Do you agree with me that here, as part of the order for engineering support, you order that a passage be made through your own and through enemy minefields?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're issuing this order to them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The focus of engineering support is what I'm saying in this task, so I'm clearly specifying what it is that they ought to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And you are giving this assignment to them, among others; is that right? If I put it to you now that the El Mujahedin Detachment did not accept such orders of yours at all and did not implement them, would I be correct? Would I be correct in saying that they did not do what they were told to do here, to make a passage through their own and through enemy minefields?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They passed through the minefields as they were attacking. Now, how they did this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just I noted that the answer to the question of my learned colleague from the witness - to the previous question - was not recorded. It was unclear to us whether indeed the El Mujahedin Detachment got a task or not. Maybe the witness has said "yes," but it's not recorded in the transcript. I'm referring to page 14, line 11, where the question ends -- sorry, line 6, where the question ends. Page 14, line 6. And no answer is recorded but just the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that they did not hear an answer if there was one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, I asked you whether this assignment was given to the El Mujahedin Detachment, among others.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to what I was asking you about before we were interrupted. Mr. Hasanagic, if I were to put to you that such orders of yours were not implemented by El Mujahedin -- and when I say "such orders," I mean orders such as with this one, to ensure that a passage is made through their own and enemy minefields -- would I be right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they set out to engage in combat, they had to have corridors allowing them to pass through. How they managed to do this is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put this document aside now. Could the document be shown D420 in connection with this. For the record, this is a document from the 35th Division command dated the 3rd of June, 1995 which says "An analysis of the Proljece 95 offensive as per engineering support." It says that it was sent to the 35th Division and the ONO --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations and training organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. I was wondering about the meaning of this. Witness, please turn to page 2 of the document. Can we see the page where the signature is and could we have the same in English. Or rather, to see the name of the person who drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my chief of engineering.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Refik Fazlic is your chief of engineers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, can we go back to --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if it says in the transcript that it's been signed, well, it's not been signed but there's just the signature block. The name of Refik Fazlic, chief of engineers is typed out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he also doesn't have a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. There is no stamp. And we will ask the witness to give us an explanation of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, look at the document, which says "Analysis of the offensive, Proljece 95." Do you recall -- Can we please have the document shown on page 1. Can we have page 1, please. I'd like us to see the ERN number too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I maybe ask my learned colleague, because it's addressed to the organ for operations and training, to ask the witness simply whether he has ever seen the document, to lay a foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was just about to have this established with the witness. I would not have missed that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the document. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. My next question is: Do you recall developing an analysis or that the chief of your staff ever developed an analysis of Proljece 95?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an analysis is produced after a -- an action is completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us explain why there is no signature or stamp. Would you agree with me that this is an internal analysis of your chief which is sent to you internally, within the division, which is sent to the operations and training organ of your division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is normally sent to the chief of operations and training, but the document ought to be signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that right? Let me ask you this. Perhaps you know something about the fact regardless of the document. Look at the last third of the document, which says: "Placing obstacles" -- Can we scroll down the English version -- or let's focus on the paragraph which says the -- that's page 2 of the English version, please. Page 2, paragraph 2 in the English version. It says: "Setting up barrier systems was slow because of lack of understanding on the part of the El Mujahedin Detachment which did not permit the setting up of barrier systems with PPM" --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Antipersonnel mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Antipersonnel mines. " ... So that only the following roads, K685, K706 and Cevaljusa village K702 were blocked with PTM"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-tank mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. So let's ignore whether this document was signed or not, but I'm asking you about this fact: Is it known to you that the El Mujahedin Detachment did not allow the barrier system to be erected as specified here with antipersonnel mines and that fact slowed down the process of establishing barriers at the newly reached lines?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true because they did not permit people to enter their area of deployment or disposition. For what reasons, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have an exhibit number assigned to this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 490, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we show the witness document -- Exhibit 442. I apologise. Not document. For the benefit of the transcript -- before that, can we have this enlarged, please, both versions. For the transcript, I'd like to say that this is a document by the 35 Division command dated 10th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, you may recall that you answered Prosecutor's questions in connection with this document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please read item 1 and item 3 of this document, because I'm going to focus my questions on these two. So items 1 and 3. Your Honours, item 3 is on page 2 of the English version. Now I would like to put it to you that in this item it says that the El Mujahedin Detachment will secure unhindered reconnaissance. And later on -- can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you reading item 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I'm reading item 1, Mr. Hasanagic. It says here: "Upon receipt of this order, the El Mujahedin Detachment will take all preparatory and organisational actions to reconnoiter." And now take a look at item 3: "The detachment will secure unhindered reconnaissance of the 328th and 329th Brigades." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at item 5, please. And it says here that: "All results of reconnaissance," et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. But I note here the translation of item 3 in the transcript. I think that it should be the other way around, not that the detachment will secure unhindered reconnaissance of the 328th and 329th Brigades but the other way around, that 328th and 329th Mountain Brigade will secure that the El Mujahedin can do this reconnaissance. I just noted this for the transcript. Maybe this can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is correct. Your Honours, I read it in the way that the Prosecutor states. My words have been translated incorrectly, but let me go back to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I read item 3 which reads: "328th and 329th Brigade will commands will ensure that the El Mujahid forces can reconnoiter without restrictions in their respective areas of responsibility." This is how I read this text; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that I asked you to take a look at item 5. It stipulates that -- under this document that all results of reconnaissance and collected information be reported by the El Mujahedin Detachment command during and after completed reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during and after.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you requested from the El Mujahedin Detachment's command such reports.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in effect, you never received such reports. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive these reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: About reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can close down this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: General, did you receive reports from the 328th Brigade and the 329th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now may the witness be shown document PT2255. For the transcript, may I say, Your Honours, that this is a document of the 35th Division command dated the 17th of July, 1995, addressed to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, can you see this document? Is the signature on it yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is not a lengthy document. Please read it silently.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask you is as follows: On the 17th of July, 1995 you demand repeatedly that the detachment submit every day their reports so that you could meet your obligations towards the 3rd Corps command. I say "repeatedly," Mr. Hasanagic, because yesterday we saw your document dated 5th of April, 1995, whereby you demanded the same thing. And now, do you agree that this document is specifically addressed to the El Mujahedin Detachment's command and that you demand reports?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would be -- it was a precedent in the division if reports did not come in and the division meted out severe punishment towards units who failed to submit their reports. Now I order the El Mujahedin Detachment to submit their reports because I had obligations toward my 3rd command -- 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I conclude that they did not observe the 5th of April order that we saw yesterday, at least by the date of the 17th of July, 1995; otherwise, you would have not sought such daily reports again.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, until this date and beyond this date and as long as the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to you, did you receive reports, combat reports, operational reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive operational reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. In the previous question, my learned colleague has mentioned -- has mentioned an order from the 5th of April. Could just this please be clarified. It's probably 5th of April, 1995. Or if my learned friend would have a PT or exhibit number, just for the record this would be nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: General, while we wait, I just wanted to -- to be sure that I understood your last question -- your last answer correctly. Even after you issued this order of 17th of July, which is on the screen now, even after that time, you still did not receive any reports from the El Mujahid Detachment, be it operational or otherwise. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You simply never received any submission from them as to what they had been doing or what they intended to do in the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Meaning the regular operational reports, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will revisit this question to clarify it, but in response to Mr. Neuner's intervention or question, may I state that we can take a look at this Exhibit 484 so that you are appraised of what I am discussing. This is the document dated 5th of April, 1995. So let's take a look at Exhibit 484.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, the -- we may look at Exhibit 484, but in the meantime what do we do with PT2255?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will dwell on it for a short while. I will ask the witness another question concerning it, and then I will seek its admission. But for your benefit, when I refer to the order dated 5th of April, 1995, so that you can see what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall this document? Yesterday we discussed the incorrect date on it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall chief of staff is responsible of collating all reports coming in from subordinated units and drafting the proper report, and I reminded him on the 17th of July of his obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in this order dated 5th of April, 1995 - and you mentioned the erroneous date - in that document, your chief of staff demands that deadlines for the submission of reports be honoured, and this included the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you recall being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we can close down this document and let's go back to the document PT2255, please? Now, Mr. Hasanagic, His Honour Harhoff asked you whether you received any reports on combat activities or on intentions. I'd like the Bench to understand this: Here we are discussing reports and operational reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we saw a plan that they submitted to you, and you do not dispute the receipt of that plan.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't dispute it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But this is another type?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is another type of document. Thank you. Reports outline combat and other activities of a unit in a preceding period of time; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day regular reports are supposed to be drafted as per military regulations, and we prescribed which items should be included in regular operational reports. And if nothing was done, the report -- daily regular report should state "we did nothing." But I had to have those reports so that I could collate my report to the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you simply did not receive such reports from the El Mujahedin Detachment neither on the 17th of July, 1995 nor in the remaining period while they were re-subordinated to you. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 491, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 464. For the record, this is an order from the command of the 35th Division dated the 6th of September, 1995 which the Prosecutor showed you while you were answering his questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this order once more, Witness. On the basis of this order, the officers of the 35th Division are to be deployed during combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we scroll up please. Can we scroll up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further up. Can we see the first sentence in the document in English, for the benefit of Their Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is my question: You're ordering the way in which the officers of the command of the 35th Division are to be -- the order in which they are to be deployed during combat activities. Is this what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 of the Bosnian version. And I believe that's page 4 in English. At any rate, item 6, Your Honours. Witness, please look at item 6 while we're waiting for the English version to show up on the screen. Now we have it. Thank you. According to this document, you assigned Mr. Muharem Ismicic to the forward command post of the El Mujahedin Detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is something we can conclude on the basis of the document. Mr. Hasanagic, if I were to put to you now that Mr. Ismicic did not spend a single minute at this forward command post, would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall. I can't confirm this. He left the IKM. Whether he was there or not, it's hard for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You were the commander of a division. Would it not be logical that in case he wasn't allowed to go over there, for him to report to you about it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that he did not report to you on this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wish to show you another document, a document shown to you by the Prosecutor. That's document number 478 -- or rather, that's an Exhibit 478. Please turn to item 2 of the document. For the record, let me state that this is a document of the 35th Division dated the 15th of September, 1995. Do you agree that it reads here that: "The 3rd, 4th, and 5th Battalions and the El Mujahedin Detachment should during the night bring the units to the meeting point and allow the troops to rest," and so on and so forth? Let me refer to the transcript now. The Prosecutor asked you on the 25th of September, on page 83, lines 16 to 18 the following question: "The units mentioned in item 2 of this order went to the meeting point, didn't they?" Answer -- you said, "Yes, into the preparatory area."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, waiting area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Waiting area. And you added the following: "If this is how it was ordered at the time." And there you were interrupted by the next question from the Prosecutor. I wish to clarify this point now. What you stated clearly in your evidence in answer to the Prosecutor's questions was that you were obeyed by the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion, that they observed your order.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you look at this order, you sent it to the 3rd, 4th, and 5th Manoeuvre Battalions and to the El Mujahedin Detachment. In answer to the Prosecutor's questions, you said clearly that the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion acted on your order. Now, my question is this: Did El Mujahedin observe your order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I was interrupted, but the units to whom the order was addressed, they were at the waiting area, and on the 16th of September - that's to say, the following day - they resumed their attacking activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, they observed your order. The detachment observed your order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at another document that was shown to you by the Prosecutor. Can we put the document we have on our screens away now. Let us look again at Exhibit 468. While we're waiting for the document to show up, this is the order of the 35th Division command at the IKM Babilon dated the 12th of September, 1995. I want to clarify one point with you. Look at the top part of the document in Bosnian. Do you see the text added in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read this out?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can it be enlarged a bit? Can we zoom in a bit? This isn't my handwriting. Somebody wrote "not forwarded."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Not forwarded." Mr. Hasanagic, I would conclude based on that that the document was not forwarded; in other words, it was not forwarded to the addressees. Would I be right in making that inference?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we close this document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the document was drafted. It was not forwarded, and as a result, nobody received the document. Nobody read it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness be shown Exhibit 465. And I will be finishing with that one quite soon. I mean this part of my examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you saw this document as well. This is a document of the 35th Division dated the 7th of September, 1995. It bears your signature. It relates to -- or rather, it is a supplement to the order for attack from the commander of the 35th Division. This is quite a short document. Could you please read it to yourself. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this document refers back to the assessment of the situation and the agreement with the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the command of the 3rd Battalion with a view to the carrying out of a task under the Farz plan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, is it not right that within the command and control line you issue orders to units? This process does not involve any sort of agreement.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since the units are one next to the other, they carry out tasks together. That's called coordinated action. It is up to them to see what the best way of proceeding is in carrying out this task. And then I issue an order to them to proceed that way. They can, however, proceed carrying out their task even without my order, because they are units of the same rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, had these been 3rd -- the 3rd and the 4th Manoeuvre Battalions instead, would they have agreed upon how to proceed or would you issue an order to them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they are carrying out orders and if they are neighbouring units, then they would proceed to carry out that task and I would issue them -- they would agree on how to proceed, and then I would issue an order to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we put this document away and I will resume my examination after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for delaying our resumption of the proceedings, but I had to consult with the Prosecutor on a matter which was very important for the continuation of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, I will move to a different topic. The Prosecutor showed you a series of documents, including a video clip concerning the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you recall watching the video clip? And I will show it to you once again. Can we have video VD9.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the benefit of the transcript, before the video shows up, it's the same video clip that the Prosecutor showed the witness on Monday. We only saw the image, the video. We have a new exhibit which also has the audio. We have distributed the transcript of the video clip also to the interpreters. Can we now play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have distributed copies of the transcript to the interpreters and we expect them to read. At any rate, we also have these transcripts for you. I invite the interpreters to read the transcript. It's D421.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the video from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they have a transcript which has the numbering V000-6511. Is that the one Madam Vidovic wants us to read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to make it quite clear, the interpreters have transcript D421, and I wouldn't want to have any confusion here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't find the transcript by that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. Can we have the transcript distributed to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Now the confusion seems to be extended. What you just provided to the Bench, Ms. Vidovic, was the version which apparently the interpreters also have; namely, Victor 000-6511.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is the video clip. Can I clarify for the transcript. This video appears under three different numbers in the records of the Prosecution. The transcript is attached to the video clip and bears number 421. We introduced the number in order to avoid confusion, since the Prosecution has three different numbers: 6899, 6511 and 1719. This is why we took the transcript and created it under number D421. According to the explanation provided by the Prosecution in relation to the transcript, we concluded that the video clip was one and the same. It took us quite a long time to work this out. I hope the interpreters now have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please play the video, then.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] We are here to define who Mujahedin are and why they came to this land. There is increasing discussion about Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters just wish to note that we are not providing an interpretation from Arabic. We are only reading the transcript as provided to us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Why they came, who brought them to this land? Who sent them? Do they receive salaries? Et cetera. Then we found it is our duty to introduce the Mujahedin to you. The Mujahedin are youth and matured men who felt the pain in their hearts while watching the defeats and disasters that happened to their Islamic nation, the last but not least what happened in Palestine and what is happening in Bosnia today. They saw how the dignity of Muslim is insulted on this land and how women raped and how children killed. When they saw all these atrocities by their own hands, they sold what they own, left their homelands and came here in order to defend Islam and Muslims. Those Mujahedin came from several countries. They do not know each other. No one should think they are here with blessings of their governments. This is not true. It is also not true they are paid by their countries to come here. They are here in response to the will of God and his prophet. The best proof that may back this argument is the graves that are located not far from here, where bodies of 40 martyrs are barred. These are martyrs among the best youth who did not spare their souls for the sake of God and in defending Islam and Muslims. They are not expecting a word of thanks, but only willing to get admitted into Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, which the God prepared for faithful Muslims. We must know that the Mujahedin fighter whom God grant victory must achieve two things: Physical preparation that includes training and weapon handling; and the spiritual preparation when he loves God, obey God and have fear from him. Such fighter does not get into the battle alone but with the company of God. The God will grant him victory and will plant the fear in the hearts of his enemies. The good believer who has a correct faith knows that the death can happen at any place, as God said in Surrat Al-Nissa', "Wherever you are, death will catch up with you." He knows that if a bomb attacks us now, it might kill all of us and if it comes in the battle front line, it will kill us there. In addition, if God wanted us to die in our homes and inside our sleeping rooms, we would die there. Therefore, the Mujahid who has correct faith knows and realise that death can come at any moment if God wanted that. Therefore, he is not afraid from death...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since obviously there was no interpretation into Bosnian, although we did provide everything that was needed to the interpreters, the Bosnian version too, I would kindly ask the witness to read it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Vidovic, while we are waiting, I would like to know who made the translation from Arabic into English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we received the interpretation, the translation, from the Office of the Prosecutor. I suppose the Prosecutor can help us in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Yes, I -- I can confirm that during the pre-trial proceedings of this case, the Prosecution employed a -- a certified Arabic translator, who handled the translation of all of the Arabic videotapes. That was done under the auspices of CLSS, who employed on a contractual basis an Arabic translator for this limited purpose. And so these were all done by the Office of the Prosecutor and disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But it is, I understand, an official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is indeed. And I will also just indicate, my learned colleague a few moments ago, in discussing the concept of three videotapes, just for the benefit of the Chamber, a number of the tapes, not just the Arabic ones but the other tapes, quite often were compilations. And what that means is that sometimes the same brief clip appears on more than one exhibited videotape simply because a number of them are compilations of -- of short clips from various places. And that's what my learned colleague was referring to when she said that this clip actually appears on three different videotapes. Our Arabic interpreter, when he encountered -- encountered such duplications indicated that on a spreadsheet that he produced which he provided to the Defence so that they know when certain material appears on more than one tape. And that's what my learned colleague referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we are on the subject of videotapes, can I raise one little point which is not related to what we are talking about. Yesterday in my office I received two videotapes: One from the Defence, the other from the Prosecution. I have refrained from watching both of them because I believe that evidence must be tendered in court. And I'm raising it because I received both of the -- one -- each from either side. I would like to get an explanation as to what those videos are about and what am I supposed to do with them, because I don't intend watching them -- I don't intend getting evidence in my office. I would intend to get it in court.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I understand it, we -- we submit a list of documents, and if it goes for a video, then we hand it to a court clerk. And since I did not know about the Plenary session yesterday, I presumed that this video was supposed to be used yesterday in court, and this is the reason why you were delivered this tape. That's my guess. I don't make it a habit of handing evidence directly into the hands of the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I understand. I just wanted to -- to understand what is -- thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour also referred to a tape from the Prosecution. The only such tape that I believe would have come from the Prosecution was an annex to our filing concerning the tape that we've sought leave to add to our exhibit list. I -- I would hope that that's the one you're referring to. That's the only one that I'm aware of that would have gone to the Trial Chamber from the Prosecution. And that was an annex to our filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, thank you so much. At least that explains it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let me explain. The Bosnian version of the tape, or the Bosnian translation that the witness is reading right now, has been received by us from the OTP as an official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you manage to read the transcript of this video that you just saw?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a question to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Mr. Hasanagic, did you read it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw this video clip for the first day, you identified Mr. Aiman. And for the other person, you said you did not know who he was. But now I'd like to ask you this, given that you've read the text of what this person is saying in the video: Please, you told us that that meeting took place sometime before Proljece II action, sometime in July. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I said the date. I said that I think it was during training, but I can't remember the exact date, but I'm sure that it was before July or before September. Maybe even before September.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. What I'd like to ask you is as follows: It is apparent that the person speaking is introducing the Mujahedin to you at this meeting. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what he was saying then, but it seems so from what I've read just now here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He explains who the Mujahedin were; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is stated here in this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He points out the fact that the people keep discussing the Mujahedin; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just for -- the Prosecution is not clear whether you're referring here to the words of Mr. Sha'ban or to the words of the speaker who makes -- who speaks on the tape, so to speak, a kind of background voice. In the lines of question you're putting to this witness, it appears to me that you're suggesting that Mr. Sha'ban has mentioned this. If they could please be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would ask the Prosecutor to refrain from mentioning names in the future. It is perfectly clear what I'm discussing right now. On the basis of the transcript that you saw, no speaker is being mentioned. We are discussing the words of who you name as Sha'ban. And since the witness has not identified that person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I don't understand you. The transcript that I have does mention the name Mr. Sha'ban and it mentions the name Colonel Fadhil Hassan Aftish and it looks as if the speaker is Colonel Fadhil Hassan Aftish.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, wait a minute. Wait a minute. Let's deal with this objection. You're objecting to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the interpreter ... Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is seen here on this sheet of paper that Anwar Sha'ban is speaking, but I don't want this to be mentioned in the presence of the witness lest he should be influenced. But I do not dispute that this is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. But then, Madam Vidovic, you have given the witness a -- a Bosnian transcript of this document. So he will have seen --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- these names, too, on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise. Your Honour, you are right. I'm completely baffled by this whole situation. Another thing, when it says "Colonel Fadhil Hassan Aftish," this is erroneous. We are discussing here Hasanagic. This is the witness's name. What appears on screen is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now you are testifying. What is written here is "Colonel Fadhil Hassan Aftish." If there is anything wrong here, let the witness correct it, not you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree - and if need be, you may be shown this video again - is it correct that you appear on that video?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You appear while the person in black outfit sporting a long beard is speaking.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We sat down while he was speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Were you the only Colonel Fadil there at that time?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the most senior officer in the area of responsibility, so I -- yes, I think I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. May I continue my line of questioning, please, now. That person, as it seems on the video, is explaining to you - this person with the long beard in the black outfit - is explaining to you who the Mujahedin are, how they arrived there, why they arrived there. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand he -- what he was saying then. Now I read this transcript and this confirms what you are saying right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, do you agree that this person is discussing faith predominantly? First that and then I'll ask you some other questions.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall at all the content or did you have a meeting on the topic of faith at that time? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this video be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The video is being marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark that for identification as 492.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hasanagic, I'm going to ask you about the phenomenon of the Mujahedin, of foreigners fighters in Bosnia. Is it true that they tried to establish very close ties with the local Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In their contacts with the population, they proselytized the importance of faith; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were particularly active on gathering the children. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some local Imams or some local clergy accepted them as such.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some local politicians as well.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At a certain point answering my questions today you said that politicians from Zavidovici influenced them. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information about that from the military security organ from the division, and one such information or report was sent to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: From the military security of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify. Who was the addressee of that information from the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the 35th Division, through security organs work from the 3rd Corps, and this included the responsibility of the 35th Division. They drafted a notice which I had no opportunity to see. That was sent, most probably the 3rd Corps command had an insight into it, and as such it was sent to the General Staff, which confirms what you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us make this clear. That intelligence or that report concerned the influence of local politicians and clergy on the Mujahedin. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a lengthy brief and it stated that they were more supportive of the Mujahedin than of the command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you say "they," could you explain?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The current authorities in power in Zavidovici and in some other places. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you mention "authorities," do you mean the civil authorities or the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civil authorities -- civilian authorities, together with the local Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I understood you as saying that the brief contained intelligence that the local authorities supported the El Mujahedin Detachment more than they did the 35th Division. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now I'm going to ask you something else about the Mujahedin. Please, you testified that the El Mujahedin Detachment was for a while re-subordinated to you, to the 35th Division. I would like to ask you the following: It wouldn't be true at all if somewhere -- someone were to think that all the Mujahedin who acted in Central Bosnia were members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am correct when I say so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct. They did not wear any insignia. It was very difficult to tell who they were, where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, you knew that in the area of Central Bosnia there were other groups of Mujahedin who never joined this detachment or who never came under your competence.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that there were Mujahedin or people with beards, as they called them, in Zeljezno Polje, in Tesanj, in Zavidovici, in Zenica, but no formal information reached me. This is something that I learned from, you know ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard it from people who were not part of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those groups were never re-subordinated to you. The only detachment that was re-subordinated to you was the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew who those groups were. I had the El Mujahedin Detachment as a unit of the 3rd Corps re-subordinated to my division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Abu Zubair al-Halili's group was never re-subordinated to you numbering 130 fighters.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The unit of Abu Zubair al-Halili did not take part in combat operations at the Vozuca during the Farz operation in September 1995 under the command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not under my command, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Provided that such a unit did take part under the command of the BH army and given that we are discussing your area of responsibility, you would have been informed of such participation, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the -- this was a corps operation which had its own axis, then I would not be in a position to be informed, but I did not hear about this unit during the preparation for that operation, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You had meetings, preparatory meetings for the preparation of the Farz operation with the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the IKM Luke.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, did you hear that Abu Zubair al-Halili is supposed to take part on the side of the BiH army in combat together with his 130 volunteers?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, did you hear that 120 humanitarian workers were supposed to take part in combat together with him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness be shown map 11 from the map book. I'll ask the witness to indicate some locations. Map 11 is in the system. If we can't retrieve it from the system, perhaps this map could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Or if I can assist my learned colleague. Map 11 has the ERN 0618-6706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, I believe you have the special pen -- Oh, yes, of course. You can't use it. My apologies. Can we just have a regular pen, then. Mr. Hasanagic, can you please indicate Borovnica for us on this map.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the place called Gradac.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that in that area of ours this place is referred to as a small town?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is off. We could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Gradic. Referred to as Gradic.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. It says "Gradac" and "Ostric." [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you show us Stog.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please show us Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, let me ask you this: In Operation Farz, you mentioned three important elevation points in your evidence. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones were they?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall in the Ozren-Vozuca area the three important elevation points?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's one.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kvrge, Podsijelovo, Blizna.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark each and every one of them, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you mark the place called Kesten.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hasanagic, if I wanted to reach Djurica Vis from Stog, can you please indicate for us the route I should take. Can you please draw that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what position?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From Stog.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stog, Kamenica, Prokop, Pejanovici [phoen], Kesten.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kesten, Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line from Stog via all the places you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stog, Prokop, Vejanovici [phoen], Maljkovici [phoen], Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you do that both ways, draw both of these routes from Stog.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One goes via Kesten to Djurica Vis, and the other one across Maljkovici to Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I wanted to go in the direction of Ozren and Doboj, how would that look like on this map?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djurica Vis, Orlovac, Podsijelovo, Ljecani [phoen] and further down.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw the route for us again.
