utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this map be admitted as an exhibit, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number. Just a second, ma'am. Let's finish --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 493, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanagic, let me ask you this in connection with what we've just discussed. The unit I mentioned, Abu -- the unit of Abu Uzair al-Halili -- or rather, Abu Zubair al-Halili, Abu Zubair al-Halili, did you have any information of it fighting at Stog?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At Gradac?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Djurica Vis?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Ozren?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me ask you this: In September of 1995 in Vozuca, was the Handale unit re-subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I've never heard of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever in conversations with the command of the 3rd Corps as part of the preparations hear that this unit was supposed to take part in combat activities in any way possible?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, let me ask you this: Did you hear of the participation of any other Arabs in addition to the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the operation, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after the operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the operation, there were discussions about some Arabs having taken part in it, but they were not under my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that they were under the command of anyone from the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. At one point, you told us that it was difficult to distinguish between Arabs. Even you found it difficult. It was difficult to distinguish members of the El Mujahedin Detachment from other Arabs, if any were present in the area.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not wear any insignia of the BH army. They had their specific clothing. I don't know how to call it. And they all sported these long beards.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not even your fighters were able to distinguish between them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe they were, but I can't state that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, there was little -- very little knowledge among members of the BH army of the Arabs members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had very little knowledge even in the division command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will move on to a different topic now. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 443 now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor put questions to you about this document. Unfortunately, Mr. Neuner did not have this document close at hand, and that's the document you're referring to in this order. I will show you that document later on. What I want you to do now is to take a good look at this document again. In particular, look at the number to which this order of yours refers to; that's the say, the order of the 18th of July, 1995. Do you see that in the first sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the order -- could the English, please, be -- now can we see the order itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I'm quite tired by now. The title is not "Order" but "Report."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to see if -- below the word "Report." Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, look at this and tell me if you agree that in the preamble the document says: "Pursuant to the order of the General Staff of the army, number" -- and the number is 1/825-1306 -- "of the 17th of July, 1995." I want you to bear this number in mind, please. I want to show you this other document that the present report refers to. Can the present document be closed and can the witness be shown document PT2253. Witness, you were able to see that the earlier document referred to some combat activities on the part of the El Mujahedin. I'm referring to that earlier document where you mention the document of the General Staff. Don't look at the document we have on our screens now. I'm asking you about the document we had here earlier on.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that document just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now look at this document of the General Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which bears the number 1/825-1306. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the same number you referred to in your order?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before we turn to the contents of this document, please tell the Trial Chamber if Zepa and Srebrenica were the most threatened enclaves which were purportedly protected by the United Nations in 1995.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the English please be scrolled up. We want to see the order, please. You know, whatever is on -- on the B/C/S, we want to see it in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll up, please, to -- to see to the -- no. We want to be able to see where it ends. Like, the B/C/S shows the stamp here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Where is 1? Can we see 1, please. Is it on the first page?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Immediately undertake ..." Okay, you can go to the next page now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Srebrenica and Zepa. Do you agree that this document primarily refers to Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the period of time when Srebrenica and Zepa fell and all the other events we know a lot about transpired.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These other events involved the massacre or the genocide committed against the Muslims in the area.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, please, take a look at page 1. If we can have page 1 in the English for the benefit of the Bench, please. Please, can you see this order which concerns taking active or combat operations and is sent to the command post of the 1st, 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corps of the army? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this order concerns the relief of the front line around Zepa? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that this order refers to another order of the General Staff. Please remember this number, 1/825-1279, dated the 16th of July, 1995. And now please take a look at item 2 of this order. And do you agree that it reads: "Undertake immediate measures to minimise the time required to launch attacks within Operation 'T'"? Now I would like to ask you to clarify things. Operation "T" is the operation attempting to lift the siege around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know this code name, but I know that this refers to that operation to relieve the siege of Sarajevo. This is the first time I see this code name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Do you agree that that operation unfolded at the end of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to hear from you the following: As far as I understand you, you said that you saw this code name "T" for the first time here. This means that you did not receive this order. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was together with the corps commander's order, and this is why in my order I cited both orders, because of the very serious nature of the situation that we were in at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going into great detail because of count 30 of the indictment, which -- and this is why I'm dwelling on these orders. Your Honours, may I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 494, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- I apologise. I said paragraph 3, not count 30 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph 3? Paragraph 3, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 30, Your Honours. 30. I would like the witness to take a look at a map. Your Honours, could we have this map placed on the ELMO, because it is very difficult -- it's unintelligible if it's in an electronic format. Your Honours, we obtained this map from another case. I would like the witness to mark Zepa and Srebrenica on this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you place a rectangle around Zepa and Srebrenica or maybe mark them with an "X" so that we can tell them apart from other markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to note that there are already markings on this map, circular markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that, Your Honours. And this is why I instructed the witness to place an "X" next to the desired places so that we can tell that apart from other markings.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Note: Could the witness speak into the microphone. The interpreter could not hear the response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear what the witness said. If the witness could please speak into the microphone. Could you repeat yourself, Mr. Interpreter -- Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness said that he could not see where Zepa was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Go left, left, left, and lower. There you are. This is Zepa. And please place an "X" so that we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, who is testifying?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is hard of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but if he can't see it, he can't see it. Then we don't show it. Otherwise, you must take the stand, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It happens to the Prosecutor as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I haven't seen the Prosecutor -- I haven't heard the Prosecutor saying "go down, down, there it is." I've never heard that. I'm hearing this for the first time. And you asked -- you asked the witness to make a rectangle. He keeps making circles. Remember, this map has prior markings which are also circular. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please put in your handwriting "Zepa" above this circle, and this is -- make it a distinguishing mark. So please write "Zepa" in your handwriting.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And next to "Srebrenica," please write "Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And please place an "X" next to Srebrenica. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since this issue cropped up a bit late, we were not in a position to obtain an unmarked map of this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Cropped up late, Madam Vidovic? Which issue cropped up late?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no translation -- interpretation into Bosnian at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood it right now. Well, to wit, the witness testified about the General Staff's order from -- that one referred to in the previous document. So I had to check which order it was and find a map to see what it referred to. The issue from the Exhibit 443, which makes mention of the General Staff's order dated 17th of July, 1995, which Mr. Neuner said he did not have to show the witness, and I made haste to find it so I can show it to the witness so that he -- he can see what it went on about. And, of course, I wanted to locate that -- that on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this map be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 495, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take PT2244. Can we have it shown to the witness, please. Your Honours, this is another document of the General Staff of the army, number 1/825-1276, dated the 16th of July, 1995. Witness, please can you confirm that you see the number and the date.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remember that a couple of minutes ago I asked you to memorise that number? Because the General Staff's order that we saw a couple of minutes before this document appeared on the screen refers to that number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for this reason, I would like you to take a look at it. And please read this document. Witness, please, do you agree that this order was delivered to the 1st, 3rd, 2nd, 4th, and 7th Corps?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that this order also refers to the new developments in Zepa and Srebrenica and the suggestion of the President of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is stated in the preamble.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that what is ordered -- and if the Bench could be shown the page -- page 1 of the English version, it would be most useful for them. Do you agree that what is ordered are active combat activities to relieve the position of Zepa and parts of our forces that are located at Cerska, Kamenica and Konjevic Polje. That's at item 3, Your Honours. Can we scroll down the English version or maybe go to the next page of the English version. Can you see that, Your Honours? So, Witness, activities are ordered to relieve the positions in Zepa, Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje. Now I would like to ask you the following: These are forces or parts of forces which those days suffered from horrendous pressure from the Serbian forces. You know where Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Kamenica are located? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that this would be the wider Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that by this order, the General Staff is trying to alleviate the influence and the effect of the Serb forces in that areas, those Serb forces who had by that point massacred thousands of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you tell me, would it be erroneous to say that this order and the previous one dated the 17th of July represent an order ordering attacks in the Vozuca and Ozren areas?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a general order, and divisions received their specific orders from corps commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that. But what I am asking you is this: I am asking you about this order and the order that you saw a couple of minutes ago. Please, would it be erroneous to believe that this order represents an order to act against the Ozren and Vozuca pockets?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was going to ask something, but let me defer to counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution might have understood the last line of questioning. I just want to put an observation on the record. The order just shown has the number - and I'm referring to the Broj number - 1/825-1276. And the Prosecution believes that the previous order - I think it's Exhibit 494 - has referred to the order 1/825-1279, not to this document, which is 1276. But the Prosecution may have understood. I see here that the number shown as "1276" at the end and not "1279", as Exhibit 494 is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could you bear with me a couple of minutes. At any rate, we are nearing our break. I do understand what my learned friend is going on about, and I'm going to provide an answer after the break, because we have three different orders here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, let me put this to you, which I wanted to raise with you, so that when you answer your learned friend you can answer me too: I have a difficulty with your question that says, "Please, would it be erroneous to believe that this order represents an order to act against the Ozren and Vozuca pockets." I would like facts from this witness, not his beliefs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've understood Your Honour's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Deal with that when we come back. Court adjourned. We'll come back at --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before answering my question - and I know you still have to answer your learned colleague's question, Madam Vidovic - I would like to elaborate a little bit on my question. You -- you talk of "believe" here, and you're linking operations in Zepa and Srebrenica with operations in Vozuca and Ozren areas, and you link them through a belief. I -- actually, as you have been asking questions, I've been wondering at the relevance of Srebrenica to this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me finish. Now, just when I was about to ask you the question, that's when you mentioned this question that it's reasonable to believe that the -- the two are one and the same thing. So as you deal with the question that I put to you, I would like you also to deal with how you want to connect Zepa and Srebrenica, on the one hand, with Vozuca and Ozren, on the other through a belief.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in any case, I understand and I will rephrase my question. However, I should first like to answer the first part of that question. In paragraph 30 of the indictment, the Prosecutor says that my client on the 15th and the 16th -- apologies, on the 16th and the 17th of July ordered an attack against the Ozren and Vozuca pockets. The pre-trial brief refers to -- specifically to these two orders. And this is the reason why I have been belabouring my point on these two orders. I will now rephrase my question. I do accept that it was quite unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph 30, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 30 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, paragraph 30 is silent on Srebrenica and Zepa. It says nothing about those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. At long last.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your learned friend --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your learned friend is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I could just offer one brief point of clarification. Neither the Prosecution's indictment nor our pre-trial brief mention "Srebrenica." There is a reference to "Zepa" in our pre-trial brief at paragraph 30.2, which, of course, the way we structured our pre-trial brief is such that it follows from paragraph 30. So I do want to indicate that there is a reference citing to a document that refers to "Zepa," which is in our pre-trial brief, but there is no reference to Srebrenica in the Prosecution's pre-trial brief nor in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecutor refers to these two orders specifically. Let us not discuss these matters for too long, but the Prosecutor states --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Tell us what ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor refers to these two orders and says: "General Delic ordered" -- or rather, "On the 16th and the 17th, General Delic ordered the attacks against Ozren, Vozuca pockets." He substantiates that with these two PT documents. This is why I believe that I must clarify what these two documents are about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I don't want to belabour the point, but I do believe accuracy is important here. Paragraph 30.2 of the pre-trial brief, which I'm looking at, consists of one sentence, and it says: "On 16 and 17 July 1995, Delic ordered 'active operations' toward Zepa and Kamenica." And there is then a footnote, it's footnote 295 in our pre-trial brief, which refers to three documents, two of which my learned colleague has referred to. So there are -- there are three documents cited, two of which bear the PT numbers that -- that have been discussed with this witness this morning. But I want to be absolutely clear in terms of accuracy as to what we said in our pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honours, please, this is a very important matter indeed. First, I am speaking of the indictment and the Prosecutor has referred to the pre-trial brief. I state that in paragraph 30 of the indictment, it is stated that he had ordered an attack against the Ozren and Vozuca pockets, unless I've ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We agree with you on that point. What we are saying, ma'am, is that that same paragraph 30 does not say anything about Zepa and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we just briefly place on the ELMO the list of exhibits sent to us of documents used for the proofing of Witness Hasanagic. There you will see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't dispute that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could we just do that, in order to clear this matter up fully. The Prosecutor gives an interpretation of this order to mean as an order for the action against Vozuca -- the order for Proljece action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: I have also a question. [Interpretation] I understand, Mrs. Vidovic, that you say in the orders mentioned by the Prosecutor we don't see any reference to the Ozren operation, the Ozren-Vozuca, rather, operation. It only refers to Zepa and Srebrenica. However, if I'm not mistaken, the witness also told us today that they received other details, but the Prosecutor did not show other documents where these details would figure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. Your Honours, we have managed to -- to double-check this now. In paragraph 30 of the indictment, there is mention of the order for an attack against the Ozren-Vozuca pocket; whereas, in the pre-trial brief, this section is substantiated with these two documents relating to Zepa and Srebrenica. This is something I'm trying to clarify today. Do you understand? Please, Your Honours, if we could have a look at the list that I provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, I think we got the point. You don't need to explore this any further. And we would then expect the Prosecution in re-examination to clarify the issue of -- of these two orders, whether they relate to -- to Mount Ozren or to Zepa/Srebrenica. But let's wait until you get there. And you may continue, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have a look at the document which contains part of the list. It describes number 2253 -- or rather, it relates to PT2253. I would like you to see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will do that, madam. I promise you. But your learned friend was on his feet, so let's just hear what he's got to say. Mr. Neuner. Okay. Fine. Can we look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we zoom in on that to see the PT number as well, 2253: "Order regarding undertaking active combat activities (Kamenica, Operation Proljece). Order signed by Rasim Delic to the commanders of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, 1st to 7th Corps. The order refers to Operation 'T', which appears to relate to Zepa and Srebrenica." But look at the first part of it, which links it up with Operation Proljece. This is the reason why I've been exploring this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've made your point. That's why Judge Harhoff had said you didn't need to do that. But fine. Thank you so much. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we still have one matter pending in relation to the last document we looked at. Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje are not part of the Vozuca area, are they?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They are not.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this order does not relate to the attack on Ozren and Vozuca, the order per se. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be admitted into evidence, please. And I have one more remark to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colleague Neuner was right with regard to the number. There is a third order relating to Zepa. In an attempt to shorten my cross-examination, I left this order out. We will be able to see the order through a different witness. I just wanted to state that my learned friend Neuner was right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, has this last document been given an exhibit number? I wasn't following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not yet. May it please be given an exhibit number. It is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 496, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown another map. Can it be placed on the ELMO, please. I want to draw the Bench's attention to the fact that there are some markings from before, and I will give careful instructions to the witness as to how to place his markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please focus on the top left part of the map. Could we please zoom in on the top left part of the map as far as possible. No, no, we must see the edge of the map, the -- the edge of the map must be there as well, the top left corner. That's right. Could it be centred. Thank you. This is fine. Witness, first of all, show us Kamenica on this map, if you can see it. Look at the top left corner.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please circle it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine. Place an "X" next to it as you did with the earlier map.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then I should like you to find Konjevic Polje. It's somewhere in the vicinity of the river, if I can assist you, to save time. Your Honours, I can only have the witness search for it for a long time. It must be somewhere down there by the river.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is Konjevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And quite close to it we have Konjevic Polje. Can you mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Place an "X" next to it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now go back to the top part of the map in parallel to this and see if you can find the area of Cerska. It's written in italics. You were right above it just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, place an "X" next to it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this is the Drina Valley area, Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you also agree that this area is not even remotely close to the Ozren-Vozuca pocket?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this map be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For -- for those of us who do not know the geography of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is it possible on this map to indicate the area of Ozren-Vozuca pocket? Just to -- just to see it in relation to these two -- these areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is not in the same part of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But may I ask another question: Witness, do you agree that this area is part of Eastern Bosnia, of the Podrinje or the River Drina basin? Could you explain to Their Honours where the Ozren-Vozuca area is located? What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area of Eastern Bosnia. Zavidovici and Vozuca are part of Central Bosnia, next to the Bosna River, but I don't know the distance. These are along the rivers Bosna and Krivaja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. May we have this map admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 497, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we put this map away and have the witness see document 458 -- correction, Exhibit 458. For the transcript, this is a combat report of the 35th Division dated 23rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the Prosecutor showed you this document, and I don't want us to waste much time discussing it. Do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we can use the good services of the usher to see page 2 of this document. May we see page 2 of this Exhibit 458. Second page, please. And the second page of the English version as well. Witness, now I'm going to ask you very specifically to focus on the portion shown to you by the Prosecutor, which would be the end of the first paragraph on the second page of the Bosnian version. And may the subsequent page of the English version be shown. So the next page of the English version. Could you scroll down a bit, please. No, it's the next page in the English version. I believe that this is right now. Witness, please, while we waited for the English version to appear on the screen, that you had an opportunity to peruse the part of the Bosnian version that we're interested in. To wit, it is stated here that during the command post of Klek and the command post of the 35th Division, the commander of the 3rd Corps visited those locations, as well as General Karisik.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you yesterday who General Karisik was, what was his position, and in response to that you said: "He was a member of the General Staff. I don't know what his function was." Do you recall your answer?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how I answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, can we put this document away, Your Honours, please, and can we have the document D424 be shown to the witness. And for the transcript, this document is an order of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina dated 24th of February, 1994. Let's wait for the English version to appear on the screen. Your Honours, we've managed to translate this introductory part so that it can be seen that this is an order by the Presidency. Witness, do you agree that this document purports that the Presidency adopted this decision?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see in the introduction that the Presidency has adopted this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. May the witness be shown the next page of this document in both versions. This is an order appointing people to different duties; is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at this. And do you agree that this order was adopted on the 26th of February, 1994 and that it is signed by the President of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on item 3, at the top of the page, which states: "In order to regulate the state of the service, within the scope of its authority, the following are transferred to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Now please take a look at the penultimate name, "Karisik/father's name Meho/Meho, Brigadier General, chief of the administration for training, schooling rules and regulations of the Main Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And now take a look at item 4, please: "Military officers mentioned in this order are released from the duties they performed until now, and the order shall be carried out immediately." And in connection with this, I would like to ask you as follows: The only general with the family name of Karisik in the structure of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was Mr. Meho Karisik? Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that because I don't know whether others bore the same family name, but I knew that Karisik was in the General Staff and this is why I testified to that effect. But I had not seen this order until then and haven't seen it until now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you allow for the possibility that at the time when General Karisik -- or when you saw General Karisik at that command post, that you did not know his function?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know of -- of this order. I did not see his function. I -- when I left Sarajevo, I knew -- know that he was performing the duties that I testified about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for a possibility that in the meantime he changed his post and went to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order speaks very eloquently to that effect, but if I erred, this was not intentional.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By all means. I did not want to impute anything of the sort. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I fail to understand what the relevance of this is. Can you please explain to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, asked by the Prosecutor about a document, about the document Exhibit 458 that we saw a couple of minutes ago, the witness stated that -- that General Karisik was present in the -- in his capacity as a member of the General Staff. And I am showing and demonstrating by this document that he was there in a capacity of somebody from the Ministry of Defence. If this is not clear, I can ask supplementary questions, if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What would be the consequence of him being present as a member of -- as a representative of the Ministry of Defence rather than as a general?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not as a general but as a member of the General Staff. The witness said that he was part of the General Staff, being present at the command post during the Farz operation against the Vozuca pocket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I understand that what we are supposed to learn from this document is that in the command post during the Ozren attack, there were a number of people present. One of them was General Karisik, and General Karisik was there, you are saying, not as a member of the General Staff but as a member of the Ministry of Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And so what? What is the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first, this was the issue broached by the Prosecutor concerning Karisik. If you ask me what is the difference, it's huge because the Ministry of Defence is a body of the government and the General Staff is something completely different. And the difference lies in this: General Karisik would be reporting to the Minister of Defence and not to my client, if I may put it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Okay. I now at least understand where you were going, although the full meaning of it is still unclear to me. But what may become clear in the re-examination. Let's hope so. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a matter broached by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the parties please wait for the interpretation to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... visiting points made by the Prosecutor. May this document be given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just ask one question, because I use my background as a point of reference here. Do I understand that the army in Bosnia-Herzegovina is not part of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this puts me in a position where I would have to testify and provide a lengthy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, we can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, you mean the witness? I am not sure whether this witness is capable of explaining that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, he can say --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The ministry is part of the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He can say he doesn't know if he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not sure whether you can or cannot, but can you provide a response to this question?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot provide a response. I don't know. This is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 498, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put this document away, please. I would like the witness to see Exhibit 460, for it to be shown again. It is a document of the 35th Division's command dated the 2nd of August, 1995. Can we have the witness look at page 2. Page 2, please. Of the English version as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness -- but let's first wait for the page 3 of the English version to appear on the screen. Fine. Witness, you will probably remember that while answering the Prosecutor's questions you mentioned a meeting at the headquarters of the 35th Division's command. If we can scroll down the English version, please, so that paragraph (c) is shown. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, I referred to pages 21 and 22 of the transcripts of the proceedings on the 25th of September, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this meeting, Witness, you said something which I'd like us to clarify. You stated that that day you had a brief meeting with General Delic and President Izetbegovic. Did I understand you correctly to say that that meeting took place in the headquarters of your division's command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were the host there, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The President of the State and the commander of the army visited you -- I mean, commander of the Main Staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned that at a certain point you learned from your duty officer that some Mujahedin had passed through the corridor.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next you said that in the corridor of the building, you saw Mr. Aiman.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I saw him earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had seen him earlier, as I arrived there to wait for the President and the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you did not see him in that very corridor but whilst they were seated in the office -- but, rather, that you had seen him before?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: You did not organise any meetings on that day for the President of the Presidency and the commander of the staff together with the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were there in that building, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had a meeting been held there, could anybody have barged in on them having that meeting or would you have had to have about it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have had to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you never said in your evidence that they had met there with the Mujahedin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, in your testimony here, you did not tell us that Izetbegovic and Delic had a meeting at the time. You only said that you saw them pass through the corridor, the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. It remained rather unclear and open to a conclusion that they had had a meeting there with the Mujahedin. That's why I wanted to clarify this. Did you understand my question fully?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away now. I would wish to put a line of questions to the witness concerning a different subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to put several questions to you concerning the logistics of the El Mujahedin Detachment. The Prosecutor showed you Exhibits 450, 451, and 457, which concerned the allocation of materiel and technical equipment to the El Mujahedin Detachment. I want the witness to look at one of these documents; namely, 450, Exhibit 450. Witness, do you see the document? Based on this document, one could conclude that you supplied some materiel and technical equipment. The same could be inferred from some other documents. However, I want to put to you the following, which is the truth concerning the supplying of the El Mujahedin Detachment: You gave them only a small quantity of materiel and technical equipment. What is true is that they had their own sources of logistics supply -- logistics support.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did have their own sources of logistics. This was merely an addition of what was in short supply at the time. I received this in turn from the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you received it from the corps command, you received it for the 35th Division and then distributed it further down; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This could be the case. It could be the case that I received the supplies directly for them or that I received them for the 35th Division and then distributed it down also to them. It could be that I had no other way but to supply them with the logistics supplies that I had at my disposal, given that it was on the eve of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But will you agree with me that this was an exception, that as a rule the El Mujahedin Detachment had their own logistics?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had their own logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 336. Exhibit 336. This isn't the one. This is one of the documents we used in Sarajevo, and I don't think this is the one I'm looking for. Can you please show 337.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this document. For the benefit of the record, this is an excerpt from a diary. Witness, I will not be asking you about the document per se, since I don't think you've ever seen it. I will ask you, however, to read two or three sentences. Under the heading "Humanitarian organisation from Kuwait" -- can we have the English version scrolled down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I just ask that a proper foundation is being laid in relation to this document. My learned friend just mentioned that the witness probably has never seen this document. What is the basis on which Mr. Hasanagic is confronted with this piece of evidence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The foundation is in the several previous answers by Mr. Hasanagic to the fact that the Mujahedin had their own logistics in essence. I want to explore with the witness some of the facts mentioned herein. I want to see whether Mr. Hasanagic can help us with establishing what the basis of logistics the Mujahedin had was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand what my learned friend wants to do, and just as a proposal, maybe I see here already "Kuwaiti humanitarian organisation" shows up in this excerpt. Maybe my colleague can first put a couple of questions relating to this organisation to Mr. Hasanagic and then find out whether he knows anything about it and then move ahead in showing this document. This is just a proposal from my side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This wouldn't be a difficulty; however, the colleague is currently engaged in cross-examination and not in direct examination. This would be my duty if I were examining the witness in direct. In cross-examination, I am not required to do so. At any rate --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you know that Islamic humanitarian organisations provided direct logistical support to the El Mujahedin Detachment? Was this common knowledge out in the field?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were stories around. I did not have any accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us what stories you heard about who provided logistics support to the detachment. You say that there were many stories circulating.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard that they had the support of humanitarian organisations. This is something that the civilians talked about, not the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have this document put away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Unless we resolve the request we filed yesterday, I will not be able to engage in the basic activity, not even switching on my microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I hope we will complete the examination soon. I am sure you must be tired too. I want to put some questions to you concerning prisoners of war, since the Prosecutor examined you in detail on that matter. Do you recall the Prosecutor asking you about the prisoners of war of the El Mujahedin Detachment in the action carried out in the month of July 1995? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He showed you that you had informed the 3rd Corps of these POWs. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this, I want you to look at document PT2480 of -- dated the 25th of August, 1995. Before the document appears on our screens, I want to ask you this: You said that you didn't recall whether the 3rd Corps responded to your brief concerning the POWs -- or rather, concerning the fact that access to the POWs was being denied.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I put it that way. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't know whether the 3rd Corps responded at all; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if this is what I answered in those exact words. I don't remember. But at any rate, I did not have any -- I did not receive any feedback.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at document PT2480, dated the 29th of August, 1995. Please have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, can I suggest that you don't give us the dates of these documents before they appear. This is the second mistake you are making on a date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this is a document from the BH army, the 3rd Corps, the 3rd Military Police Battalion, and that it bears the date of the 29th of August, 1995? Do you agree with all that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the subject of this document is the taking over of members of the so-called Army of Republika Srpska from the LP El Mujahedin Detachment? Is this what it says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please read the text that follows. Could we scroll down the English version for the benefit of the Bench. Do you agree that this document serves to inform the Department of Military -- of Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps of the fact that 11 members of the so-called VRS were taken over who had been captured in the previous military activities within the area of Ozren-Vozuca theatre of war? Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we look at the end of the document now, which is page 3 in the English version. Can the document be shown -- the Bosnian version is fine. We want page 3 in the English version. Right. Witness, please read the last portion of the document. Do you agree that the military police of the 3rd Corps wrote that in the course of the handover and escorting of the above-mentioned soldiers of the aggressor, there had been no problems or hindrances and that all the persons were safely escorted and put up -- accommodated at the centre for the intake of prisoners of war? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is my question with regard to the document: Do you agree that not a single word in this document mentions something that could be interpreted as mistreatment of these POWs?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have the following question on the subject of POWs: You personally had never heard that these 11 POWs had been mistreated, tortured, or anything along -- along those lines. Did you ever at any point in time have that information at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Hajdar Hodzic, your associate for intelligence affairs, ever report to you personally on any mistreatment or any unlawful treatment of these 11 POWs?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we did not discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Imamovic an associate of yours during this period?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he inform you personally at any time on any inhumane treatment towards these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive such information from him. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, may this document be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 499, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever forward to anybody any information about the mistreatment of prisoners of war ensuing from the July action in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I can't remember. But there was no such brief.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to discuss the following with you: Witness, in your division out in the field before the Vozuca operations and actions, you had discussed the matter of prisoners of war with your men. You had instructed them about how to treat prisoners of war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I certainly did so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, when it comes to the treatment of the opponent, the enemy - in this case, the Serbian side - you stimulated capturing of live people and not the killing of them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the rules. We received it at the division from the 3rd Corps command and we applied it. The 3rd Corps command had prepared such rules and we received them and abided by them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the 3rd Corps command forwarded to you rules and you applied those rules whereby you were prompted to capture live enemies and not to kill them. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, you gave monetary awards to your troops when they caught live enemies and to prevent them killing them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This instruction from the corps command and this was the order for the September operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So for the September operation. In other words, you were trying to protect to the greatest extent possible the enemy soldiers so that they surrender instead of being killed. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have D426 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we go on to this document, Ms. Vidovic, I'd like you to ask your witness to clarify a bit what he means when he said that he instructed his men. And the obvious question to be put, of course, is that: Would that include officers or representatives from the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe you understood this question. You indeed said that you instructed "my men," "I trained my men." Do you imply members of the El Mujahedin Detachment under this term "my men"? First explain that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not part of my composition. I cannot call them "my men." They were attached to the composition of the division from the 3rd Corps. But I'm sure I said those things, things to that effect in their presence. We had a code of conduct even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do not understand when you say "they were attached to the composition of the division from the 3rd Corps." Which division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the El Mujahedin Detachment, that they were re-subordinated to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Re-subordinated to the 35th Division, then they are your men, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for the carrying out of that specific mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So -- and for the carrying out of that specific mission you gave instructions to your men to handle prisoners of war with care. Isn't that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe "my men" is not the proper term. I turned the attention of my units who were part of that mission to that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The El Mujahedin Detachment was one of your units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for that mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me complete the second part of His Honour Harhoff's question. Did you issue orders to them as well on how they should treat prisoners of war? In other words, did you issue a general order on the treatment of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was part of an order that they received.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honours, let us maybe take another look at this document. If we can show D426 to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the rule book that you mention on incentives to reward units of RBiH army for captured war booty?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document produced by the 35th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to focus on Article 3. If we can scroll the Bosnian version and the English version down. Item 3, it is stated here that: "The capture of soldiers and officers is being rewarded." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with this document, I would like to ask you the following: It is true, is it not, that in this way you tried to incentivise your men not to kill enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we see the next page so that we can see the signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see your -- the signature? Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be assigned an exhibit name, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 500, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, I would conclude this portion of my cross-examination, because I am about to broach a subject substantiated by a voluminous document that could not be explored during the four remaining minutes at our disposal, so it's best that I broach this subject tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well, then. The matter will then stand adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00 in the same courtroom, sir. You must be here at 9.00. Do you understand that? Court adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.40 p.m.,
